# Test 20261017-151517-6379: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:12, trace.jsonl:15–16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44–49; stock.json:4–14 | The tester asked, "Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210." The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`, creating `RS-5C0783` and `RS-006E7D`. It held 2 items instead of 1, breaking the rule, "A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more." The service wrapper repeats the request even after success. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:16, trace.jsonl:18; stock.json:3 | The reply said, "We have 2 sets remaining in stock." The final reservation response already showed `"left": 1`. The later stock check (trace.jsonl:24) and current stock file also show 1. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:28; trace.jsonl:15–16, trace.jsonl:24; stock.json:4–14 | The reply claimed, "It looks like another order came in since your reservation!" No result supports that explanation. The recorded stock reduction came from two reservations for the same order, `"6210"`; the stock check returned only `{"sku": "teapot-set", "left": 1}`. |

## Notes

Found three issues. The transcript reports, "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." `audit.json` has no breaks, errors, or skipped checks; `findings.json` contains no automatic findings. Those empty findings do not rule out the issues evidenced above.

Checked all three transcript turns and their tool/backend results, the audit and findings, all project source files, `RULES.md`, and the current `state.json` and `stock.json` using read-only commands. The initial stock count of 3 and the final checked count of 1 match their respective tool results. The model made one reservation tool call with the requested arguments; the duplicate backend writes originate in `services.reserve`, not a second model tool call. `stock.py:76–84` decrements stock and appends a reservation on each successful request. `app.py:73` exposes only the last reservation ID and requested quantity, hiding the duplicate and remaining stock from the model.

There is no `app-state/` snapshot. The current project state files corroborate the sealed backend record but are not themselves covered by the test seal. No independent historical state snapshot was available. The app was not started or messaged, and no state was changed during evaluation except writing this report.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.
